content.text: {"what_it_is":{"claims":[{"text":"The Virginia Class Submarine (VCS) program funds construction of the U.S. Navy's nuclear-powered attack submarines under the 'Shipbuilding and Conversion, Navy' account, and is categorized as a shipbuilding program.","citation":{"fact_id":"a46814a7c44e6bdc"}},{"text":"The stated mission of these submarines is to seek out and destroy enemy ships across a wide spectrum of tactical scenarios, operating either independently or with a battle group, and to provide covert striking power against targets ashore, the ability to establish an expeditionary force on land, and the maritime strength to destroy enemy naval forces and interdict seaborne commerce.","citation":{"fact_id":"cf2850271c560361"}},{"text":"For fiscal year 2026, the Department requests a total of $11,078,029 thousand (about $11.1 billion) for a total quantity of 2 ships.","citation":{"fact_id":"a46814a7c44e6bdc"}},{"text":"That FY2026 total is split into $3,943,521 thousand of discretionary funding for one ship and $7,134,508 thousand of mandatory (reconciliation) funding for one ship.","citation":{"fact_id":"cf2850271c560361"}},{"text":"The mandatory funding pays for one FY2026 submarine plus continued investments in nuclear shipbuilder productivity wage enhancements, while the discretionary funding covers one FY2026 submarine along with advance procurement and economic order quantity funds for future submarines.","citation":{"fact_id":"ab7edeece9637c51"}},{"text":"The program is currently executing its fourth Multi-Year Procurement (MYP) contract, known as Block V, which was awarded on 2 December 2019, modified on 22 March 2021 to add a tenth submarine, and modified again on 30 April 2025 to include the FY2024 eleventh and twelfth submarines.","citation":{"fact_id":"cf2850271c560361"}},{"text":"Block V submarines incorporate the Virginia Payload Module (VPM), an 84-foot hull section with four additional payload tubes, each capable of carrying seven Tomahawk cruise missiles or other payloads, beginning with hull SSN 803.","citation":{"fact_id":"cf2850271c560361"}},{"text":"The VPM is intended to help mitigate the loss of undersea strike capability that will come with the planned retirement of the Navy's four guided missile submarines (SSGNs) in the late-2020s.","citation":{"fact_id":"cf2850271c560361"}},{"text":"The program is also planning its fifth Multi-Year Procurement contract, Block VI, covering procurements from FY2025 through FY2029.","citation":{"fact_id":"cf2850271c560361"}}]},"why_it_matters":{"claims":[{"text":"The program is a large and growing line: actual spending in FY2024 was $10,656,927 thousand (about $10.7 billion).","citation":{"fact_id":"8200475b25ef456f"}},{"text":"For FY2025, enacted funding was $13,320,211 thousand (about $13.3 billion).","citation":{"fact_id":"f8c1af9fefe2b7fa"}},{"text":"The FY2026 request of $11,078,029 thousand represents an increase over the FY2024 actual level of $10,656,927 thousand.","citation":{"fact_id":"7236e3bef5d0313a"}},{"text":"FY2026 funding includes $130 million of Submarine Industrial Base (SIB) investment for construction spares to help de-risk schedules, plus $817 million of full funding for advance procurement and economic order quantity for future submarines.","citation":{"fact_id":"ab7edeece9637c51"}},{"text":"FY2026 also funds completion of prior-year shipbuilding programs to cover the Government's share of contract cost overruns: $121.5 million for the FY2016 SSNs 796 and 797, $99.1 million for the FY2017 SSNs 798 and 799, and $289.8 million for the FY2018 SSNs 800 and 801.","citation":{"fact_id":"ab7edeece9637c51"}},{"text":"The April 2025 contract modification drew on funds from the American Relief Act of 2025 (H.R.10545) — $1,950 million to support FY2024 hulls, $1,528 million for the FY2025 hull, and $2,213 million for shipbuilder workforce support and infrastructure enhancements.","citation":{"fact_id":"cf2850271c560361"}}]},"players":{"claims":[{"text":"Lobbying filings from General Dynamics Corporation reported lobbying for full funding of the Virginia Class and Columbia Class submarine programs and funding for the submarine industrial base.","citation":{"fact_id":"2e0033079e665cda"}},{"text":"Additional 2025 filings from General Dynamics Corporation similarly referenced lobbying for full funding of the Virginia Class and Columbia Class submarine programs.","citation":{"fact_id":"abf01fdb5491c25b"}},{"text":"Filings from General Dynamics also referenced monitoring issues related to military equipment sales to key nations and the Australia–United Kingdom–United States (AUKUS) partnership.","citation":{"fact_id":"0a31d8443c8e12ac"}},{"text":"Lobbying filings from Huntington Ingalls Industries Incorporated referenced the Virginia Class Submarine (VCS) among a list of Navy programs including the Carrier Replacement Program, CVN RCOH, DDG-51 class multi-year procurement, DDG(X), LHA, LPD Flight II, and Columbia class.","citation":{"fact_id":"031b3d01352d06c2"}},{"text":"A 2025 Huntington Ingalls Industries filing likewise referenced the Virginia Class Submarine among its list of Navy programs.","citation":{"fact_id":"0568ff737bab3630"}}]},"recent_developments":{"claims":[]}}
